subject: Tool choreography & fallbacks — integration next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tool choreography & fallbacks — integration next steps

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good signal on the payer-lookup and appointment-scheduler use cases. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Recap (what we heard):
  * You need an NLU + structured output pipeline to convert unstructured patient messages into a canonical appointment request
  * Lookup tools: internal EHR search and external payer verification (parallel checks)
  * Must meet HIPAA controls and have strict auth/KMS for any PHI-handling requests
  * Reranking/search: embeddings to surface best matches from patient history

- Suggested integration approach (high-level):
  1) SDK integration for calls and structured output: use Redwood SDK to call model -> request a JSON schema (we'll provide examples)
  2) Tool definitions: two tool wrappers (EHRRead, PayerVerify) called in parallel with a 1.5s soft timeout; when both succeed we merge results; if one fails, fallback to cached lookup + signal to retries queue
  3) Auth/routing: short-lived tokens via your IdP (OIDC) for API calls, key material in KMS/HSM for model access; traffic routed to our Dedicated pool in us-west for latency guarantees
  4) Embeddings & reranker: periodic offload to embeddings pipeline (batch updates nightly) + on-demand rerank with top-k candidate expansion

- Risks we flagged: vendor API rate limits (we recommend exponential backoff + jitter in the tool wrapper), schema mismatches (we'll add a strict validator step), PHI in logs (disable telemetry for PHI routes).

Next steps / asks: 
- Dev: Can you share a sample EHR API spec and a representative appointment message payload? (Jordan)
- Security: Acero security to confirm acceptable KMS options and JWE/JWT expectations (Jordan / sec@acerohealth.com)
- Schedule: propose a 60m technical workshop with Dev + Marcus next week to workshop tool wrappers and the schema. (Calendly link below)

I've attached a short playbook that outlines our proposed tool patterns and a brief checklist for HIPAA-sensitive endpoints. If that looks good I'll draft a MAP and we can lock in the workshop time.

Attachments: redwood-playbook-tool-patterns.pdf

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Tool choreography & fallbacks — integration next steps

Thanks, Evelyn — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) HIPAA / Auth: We prefer using our existing AWS KMS with cross-account grants for encryption-at-rest, and OIDC for short-lived service tokens. Are those supported? Our security team (cc'ed) will want specifics on key rotation and audit logging.

2) Parallel checks: the payer verification endpoint has burst limits; we can increase quota for the pilot but need a fallback if we hit 429. Your soft timeout + cached-response sounds reasonable.

3) Data residency: All PHI must stay in us-west for the pilot. Can you ensure routing to that region?

I've attached a one-page EHR API spec (excerpt) and a sample appointment message. Will share the full OpenAPI next week if helpful.

Regards,
Jordan Miles
Product Manager, Integrations | Acero Health
[jordan.miles@acerohealth.com]

Attachments: (inline) sample-appointment-payload.json (referenced, scope-limited)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tool choreography & fallbacks — integration next steps

Jordan — great, thanks for the spec excerpt. Short technical notes and a proposed MAP (attached):

- Auth & KMS:
  * We support customer-managed KMS; for Hosted/Dedicated we can accept wrapped keys or cross-account grants. For Private we can plug into your HSM.
  * For API calls, our SDK supports OIDC token exchange and mTLS; short-lived session tokens are recommended to avoid long-lived secrets in tool wrappers.

- Tool wrapper pattern (pseudo):
  * Tool definition: name, input_schema, timeout_ms, retry_policy, error_mapping
  * Execution: fan-out to EHRRead + PayerVerify concurrently, collect futures, apply 1.5s soft timeout, then apply deterministic merge strategy (prefer EHRRead for patient fields; PayerVerify for insurance fields)
  * On 429/5xx from external: retry up to 2 times with exponential backoff; if still failing, return best-effort cached response and flag for async recheck

- Structured output: we'll provide a JSON Schema v1 that the model must emit. Please confirm the set of fields you need (patient_id, preferred_times, insurance_token, urgency_score).

- Embeddings/reranker: nightly batch to update vectors (S3 staging, redwood embeddings store), then an inline rerank step that calls the model with top-20 candidates. Rerankers will be run in Dedicated to meet latency SLOs.

- Proposed MAP (high level):
  1) Week 0: Technical workshop (60m) — draft tool definitions and validate schema
  2) Week 1: Dev pilot — implement wrapper + smoke tests against sandbox EHR
  3) Week 2: Pilot with limited traffic (us-west) + security sign-off
  4) Week 4: Production rollout & SLA handoff

I've attached an initial MAP spreadsheet you can use to track owners and milestones. I'll set up the tech workshop — tentative slots on the Calendly link below.

Attachments: MAP-AceroHealth-v1.xlsx

—Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
